General Staff Confirms Strikes on Engels Airbase and Saratov Refinery — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine confirmed that defense forces struck the Engels strategic airfield and the Saratov oil refinery in Russia early Sunday, Aug. 2. The military noted that the Engels base houses Tu-95MS and Tu-160 bombers used to attack Ukraine. Concurrently, long-range Ukrainian drones struck the Bashneft-UNPZ oil refinery in Ufa, Bashkortostan, located over 1,700 kilometers (1,056 miles) from t

Ukrainian Drones Destroy 8 Russian Radar and Air Defense Sites — The 1st Separate Center of the Unmanned Systems Forces (USF) of Ukraine reported executing pinpoint strikes more than 270 kilometers deep into the Russian Krasnodar Krai, destroying eight critical aerial surveillance and defense assets. The targets included a TOR-M2 surface-to-air missile system and various radar stations, including Nebo, Gamma, and Kasta systems, located across Yeysk, Primorsko-Akhtarsk, Kamyshevatskaya, Pryhybsky

Air Defenses Downed 445,000 Russian Targets Since 2022 — Acting Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara stated on Ukraine’s Air Force Day that air defense units have intercepted over 445,000 Russian aerial targets since February 2022, including cruise and ballistic missiles, and drones. Additionally, Ukrainian aviation has conducted over 38,000 combat sorties, destroying more than 12,000 threats. US Pauses Planned Strikes on Iran Amid Deal Talks — US President Donald Trump announced the suspension of a planned 10-to-14-day military campaign against Iran following requests from Tehran and regional states to rapidly negotiate a deal. Trump stated that the agreement must include the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the cessation of Iran’s nuclear program, noting that Israel supports the pause. The sudden de-escalation follows US State Department warnings for citizens to leave

Ukraine Deploys Firefighters to France Amid EU Wildfires — Ukraine has dispatched firefighters to France for the first time under the EU Civil Protection Mechanism to help combat large-scale wildfires raging near Bordeaux. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen highlighted the deployment as a sign of European solidarity amid Ukraine’s ongoing defense against Russian forces. Southern Europe is facing severe wildfires due to temperatures exceeding 40 degrees Celsius, with several EU na

Drones Strike Saratov Refinery and Samara Wildberries Hub — Ukrainian drones struck a major oil refinery in Saratov and a Wildberries logistics center in the Samara region early Sunday, Aug. 2. The Saratov strike sparked a large fire, marking the 15th attack on the facility, which previously had operations halted by a July strike. In Samara, a 178,600-square-meter Wildberries hub was targeted, continuing a sustained campaign that has destroyed approximately 38% of the Russian e-commerce giant’s

Polish Police Arrest Suspect in Attack on Ukrainian Woman — Police in the Polish city of Gdynia arrested a 76-year-old man on Saturday, Aug. 1, in connection with the July 30 assault on a 40-year-old Ukrainian woman. The suspect allegedly struck the victim twice on the back of the head with a wooden cane before fleeing. The woman was treated for non-life-threatening injuries and discharged. Regional police stated there is currently no evidence linking the attack to national hatred.

Blast at Moscow Restaurant Kills 3 Amid General’s Party — An explosion at the Balzi Rossi restaurant in central Moscow on Saturday evening killed three people and injured 21 others. The Russian National Antiterrorism Committee stated that a woman attempted to carry an improvised explosive device into the venue but was stopped by a security guard; both died in the blast alongside one patron. The restaurant was hosting a birthday celebration for a Russian general, supported by the presence of mili

Russian Strikes Hit Kharkiv and Mykolaiv, Injuring 6 — Russian drone strikes targeted Kharkiv and the Mykolaiv region early Sunday morning, injuring at least six people, including three children. In Kharkiv, overnight strikes hit the Industrialnyi, Kyivskyi, and Saltivskyi districts, damaging a high-rise building and causing acute stress reactions in three residents (a 74-year-old man, an eight-year-old girl, and a 13-year-old boy). This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Beyond Borders: Oleksandr Dubovyk’s Universe — As Kyiv prepares to open The Triumph of the Bouquet, a landmark exhibition dedicated to Oleksandr Dubovyk, the 95-year-old artist reflects on freedom, culture, war, and the future of humanity. His words reveal not only one of Ukraine's most influential painters, but also an original philosophical voice whose ideas reach far beyond art.

Ukrainian Drones Sink Russian Ship Yanina, Hit 3 Ufa Refineries — Ukrainian drones conducted a massive coordinated operation early Saturday, August 1. Naval drones sank the Rosatom-affiliated container ship Yanina, a sanctioned vessel with a capacity of over 100,000 tons, approximately 130 miles from Novorossiysk. Concurrently, long-range SBU drones struck three major Bashneft oil refineries in Ufa, Bashkortostan, located 1,600 kilometers from the border, with a combined capacity of over 23 mill
Ukraine at 35: The Fedorov Affair and the Test of Ukraine’s Democratic Maturity — What a minister’s dismissal has revealed about the good, bad, and pending in Ukraine’s democracy.

Latvia Closes Belarus Border — Latvia temporarily suspended border crossings with Belarus on Friday evening due to an information system failure at the Pāternieki checkpoint. Interior Minister Jānis Dombrava urged travelers to use alternative routes. The national cybersecurity agency, CERT.LV, stated there is no indication of a cyberattack or external interference.

Russian ‘Rassvet’ Satellites Secure Two Daily Comms Windows Over Ukraine — The first batch of 16 Russian “Rassvet” satellites, launched by Bureau 1440 in March 2026, has reached its operational orbit and is currently providing at least two daily “communication windows” over Ukraine, each lasting over an hour. According to satellite communications expert Volodymyr Stepanets, while the satellites pass over Ukraine four times a day, only two or three passes are high enough to ensure stable connecti

HUR Drones Strike Russian Pantsir System and Boat in Crimea — Operators from Ukraine’s Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR) struck a Russian Pantsir-S1 air defense system in the Kherson region, alongside a Project 1100M Sargan boat in Kerch and a Forpost drone control station in Yevpatoria on the night of July 30. The HUR estimated the value of the Pantsir-S1 at $15 million and the Sargan boat at $6 million.

Belarus Designates Polish Press Agency Website ‘Extremist’ — The regime of Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko has designated the website of Poland’s state-owned news agency, PAP, as “extremist” in a move slammed by leading Belarusian opposition figures.

Trump Threatens Iran With Heavy Strikes on Energy Targets — US President Donald Trump threatened to hit Iran “very hard,” with US media reporting that Washington and Israel are coordinating potential joint strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, including oil refineries and power plants, as soon as this weekend. The reports follow a recent meeting between Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Washington. The potential attacks come five months into the ongoing conflict, which b

Russian Drone Strike on Rozetka Depot in Brovary Kills 1 — A Russian daytime drone strike hit a logistics center belonging to the e-commerce company Rozetka in Brovary on Aug. 1, killing a 61-year-old man and injuring six others. The attack also damaged warehouse facilities and at least 12 vehicles. In a separate incident, a strike in the Bucha district injured three people and caused a fire at an industrial facility. These daytime attacks followed a massive barrage involving 35 missiles and 185

US to Seek Resumed Kyiv-Moscow Talks, Rubio Says — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced that Washington will intensify diplomatic efforts in the coming weeks to determine if peace negotiations between Ukraine and Russia can resume. Rubio noted that both sides maintain rigid “red lines” that must be brought closer together. The renewed diplomatic push coincides with expected visits to Kyiv by US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner later in August, marking their first trip to the U

Russian Drone Strikes High-Rise in Odesa, Injuring 3 — A Russian attack drone has struck a multi-story residential building in the center of Odesa, injuring three people, according to local authorities. Both victims were hospitalized with thermal burns. The strike on Odesa follows a massive nationwide barrage on Saturday, during which Russia launched 35 missiles and 185 attack drones. During the overnight attack, Ukrainian air defenses intercepted only one of 27 ballistic missiles due to a criti

Convicted of Child Sexual Abuse, He Was Sent to Ukraine Anyway — At times the desire not to be associated with bad news coming out of Ukraine keeps organizations from doing the right thing. In Norway, one aid organization allowed a convicted sex offender to travel to Ukraine while his case was being appealed.

Ukraine Strikes Crimean Rail Bridges and Naval Drone Depot — Ukraine’s General Staff confirmed a series of strikes on Aug. 1 against Russian military targets in Crimea, the Kherson region, and the Zaporizhzhia region. In Crimea, Ukrainian forces hit a naval drone storage facility near Chornomorske, the Syvash railway bridge near Chonhar, a railway bridge near Vladyslavivka, a Black Sea Fleet electronic intelligence unit in Sevastopol, and a repair base in Pervomaiske. Additional strikes targeted

Russian Attack on Kyiv Damages Lithuanian Embassy, 25 Ambulances — A massive Russian missile and drone attack on Kyiv damaged the Lithuanian embassy and a medical transport depot, destroying five ambulances and significantly damaging 20 others on Saturday morning. Ukrainian officials confirmed the strike caused major disruptions to the city’s medical fleet. The broader attack killed nine residents and injured 30 others across seven districts, as air defenses struggled with a critical shortage of

Drone Barrage Hits Ufa Refineries and Crimea Bases — On Saturday, Aug. 1, a massive Ukrainian drone strike targeted Russian oil refineries in Ufa, Bashkortostan, and military positions in occupied Crimea. The Russian Defense Ministry claimed to have intercepted 274 drones across 16 regions. In Ufa, flight operations were restricted as fires broke out at refinery facilities. In Crimea, satellite imagery confirmed fires at a Black Sea Fleet electronic warfare center on Cape Fiolent and an air defe

Ukraine Downs Only 1 Ballistic Missile During Massive Attack on Kyiv — A massive overnight Russian attack involving 35 missiles and 185 drones resulted in at least nine deaths and 30 injuries in Kyiv. Due to a critical shortage of Patriot interceptors, Ukrainian air defenses were only able to shoot down one ballistic missile. The strikes affected seven districts in the capital, damaging 18 residential buildings, educational facilities, and the Lithuanian embassy. Attacks also targeted the Dnipro

Explainer: Why Kyiv’s Shelters Fail Civilians Under Russian Attack — Bureaucratic delays, geography and outdated architecture have left Ukraine without enough adequate shelters. Even where protection is available, the realities of a high-intensity war often discourage civilians from using it.

Russian E-Commerce Prices Surge After Wildberries Strikes — Prices for goods on major Russian online marketplaces, primarily Wildberries and Ozon, have surged by 10% to 30% in recent days following a series of Ukrainian drone strikes targeting logistics infrastructure. The price hikes are driven by the sudden cancellation of platform-funded discounts as companies attempt to cover losses and rebuild supply chains. Delivery times have also doubled.

Polish F-16s Intercept Russian Il-20 Plane Over Baltic Sea — Two Polish F-16 fighter jets intercepted a Russian Il-20 reconnaissance aircraft flying over the Baltic Sea approximately 40 kilometers north of Kołobrzeg on July 31. Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz confirmed the aircraft remained in international airspace but was flying without a flight plan and with its transponder deactivated. The interception follows a July 30 incident in which a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile entered Pol

Zelensky Updates NSDC Roster Amid Government Reshuffle — President Volodymyr Zelensky updated the composition of Ukraine’s National Security and Defense Council (NSDC) on July 31, bringing in new key leadership following a major government reshuffle. The newly appointed members include Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapatyi, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi, and several ministers and acting agency heads, such as Yevhenii Khmara and Andrii Sybiha.

Ukrainian Woman Assaulted in Polish City of Gdynia — A 40-year-old Ukrainian woman was assaulted from behind with a wooden cane in Gdynia, Poland, on July 30, requiring a brief period of hospitalization. Police are reviewing surveillance footage to identify the suspect, described by witnesses as an elderly man, though a xenophobic motive has not been officially confirmed. The incident has occured amid a documented rise in anti-Ukrainian hostility in Poland, following a recent diplomatic dispute

Trump Claims US Can Take ‘Whatever We Want’ from Ukraine Mines — US President Donald Trump stated in an interview with Real America’s Voice that the critical minerals deal signed with Kyiv allows the US to access Ukraine’s rare earth resources “at any time” and take “pretty much whatever we want,” valuing the agreement at over $300 billion. The bilateral deal, signed in April 2025, actually establishes a 50/50 revenue-sharing recovery fund managed by the US Development Finance Corporation and Uk

Pentagon to Hand Ukraine Aid Command to NATO Ally – Politico — The Pentagon plans to transfer leadership of the command coordinating weapons deliveries and training for Ukraine to another NATO member, Politico reported. Officials said the change should not disrupt military assistance.

Toys and Flowers Cover the Ruins as Radushne Mourns Family Killed by Russian Missile — Six of 10 members of the Voronov family were killed when a Russian missile destroyed their home in Radushne on July 30. President Zelensky said preliminary evidence indicated that Russia used a North Korean ballistic missile.

3 Women Hospitalized After Another Russian Drone Strike on Kharkiv — A Russian drone strike on Kharkiv’s Nemyshlianskyi district injured three women aged 41, 47 and 71. The attack followed two earlier drone strikes on the city’s Saltivskyi district.

The Father, the Daughter and the Kremlin: Why Putin Wants Zhanna Nemtsova in Jail — A Moscow court has ordered Zhanna Nemtsova’s arrest over her work with the foundation honoring her murdered father, Boris Nemtsov. The case shows how the Kremlin still fears his democratic legacy and his opposition to Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Fire Breaks Out at St. Basil’s Cathedral on Moscow’s Red Square — A fire broke out in the director’s office at Moscow’s St. Basil’s Cathedral early Saturday, burning an area of about 10 square meters. Around 10 fire engines responded, and the blaze was extinguished without injuries.

9 Killed, 30 Wounded as Russia Pounds Kyiv With Ballistic Missiles — A mass Russian ballistic missile attack killed nine people and wounded 30 across five Kyiv districts. Seven were killed in Darnytskyi, while rescuers evacuated 35 people from a damaged residential building in Solomianskyi.

Trump Casts Doubt on Ukraine Patriot Production License — Donald Trump said Washington has not approved licensed Patriot interceptor production in Ukraine, citing concerns over sharing advanced US weapons technology. His remarks represent a retreat from his July commitment as Kyiv urgently seeks protection from intensifying Russian ballistic missile attacks.

Sybiha, Kallas Discuss Black Sea Security, Agree on More Pressure Against Russia — Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha held a call with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas on Friday, briefing her on recent Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities and Black Sea shipping. The two also discussed Ukraine’s defense needs and recent diplomacy with Iran.

General Staff of AFU Reports 207 Combat Clashes in 24 Hours — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) reported 207 combat clashes over a 24-hour period on Friday, July 31, reporting heaviest fighting near Pokrovsk, where the AFU repelled 28 enemy attacks. Russian forces carried out 55 airstrikes and nearly 2,000 shellings nationwide.

Poland Summons Russian Ambassador After Cruise Missile Incident — Poland summoned Russia’s ambassador after a Kh-101 cruise missile struck its territory during Russia’s overnight barrage that fired roughly 20 missiles towards Ukraine. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced the diplomatic step on Friday, July 31.

Zelensky, Vance Talk Patriots Amid Trump Uncertainty — President Volodymyr Zelensky said he held a “positive and productive” call with US Vice President JD Vance on Friday, July 31, regarding the Patriot interceptors. Their call came just hours after US President Donald Trump appeared to soften an earlier commitment to let Ukraine manufacture the missiles domestically.

Thousands of Protesters Fill Central Kyiv, Call for Continued Reforms, Fedorov’s Return to Government — Tens of thousands of protesters marched through central Kyiv on Friday, July 31, demanding the reinstatement of former Minister of Defense Mykhailo Fedorov, continued reforms, and greater government accountability. Demonstrators called Fedorov’s dismissal a fatal mistake by authorities.

Ukraine Investigates Ammo Detonation at Khmelnytskyi’s Special Forces Training Ground — Ammunition detonated at a military training ground in western Ukraine’s Khmelnytskyi injured four servicemen and left several out of contact on Friday, July 31. Ukraine’s State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) and Prosecutor General’s Office have opened criminal proceedings.

Ukrainian Strikes Target 60% of Wildberries’ Warehouse Capacity — Ukrainian forces have struck at least 18 Wildberries warehouses over the past two weeks, targeting logistics facilities totaling more than 1 million square meters – 38% of the Russian online retailer's largest warehouse capacity, according to an analysis by Russian outlet Agentstvo. Including attempted strikes, 60% of Wildberries' major logistics capacity has been targeted. Ten of the company's 26 largest warehouses have been dama

EU Races to Contain New Migrant Crisis as Thousands Cross Into Spain’s N. Africa Enclave — Around 60,000 migrants have crossed from Morocco into Ceuta by swimming to the small Spanish enclave in North Africa. Spain’s interior minister said that 25,000 people who had crossed had voluntarily returned to Morocco.

Russian Aerospace Force Loves Glide Bombs It Drops on Ukraine With Impunity — Russia’s Air Force sharply increased glide bomb usage vs. Ukraine, averaging 250/day Jan-Jun 2026 (up 45%). UMPK-fitted FAB bombs, launched from 60 miles away, often miss and devastate civilian areas, killing/wounding many. Ukraine’s limited defenses leave Russia free to drop ~100,000 more by 2027 and early modern fighter deliveries.

Assassination Attempt on Top Ukrainian Commander Foiled, Khartiia Vows Battlefield Revenge — Khartiia Corps are pledging revenge on the battlefield after an alleged attacker and accomplice were detained following an assassination attempt on commander Ihor Oboliensky.

Patriot Shortages Let 3 Out of 4 Russian Ballistic Missiles Slip Through in July — Kyiv Post asserted that Russia had launched a record 377 missiles at Ukraine in July as of the afternoon of July 31. Of those, 251 were cruise missiles and 126 were ballistic missiles, with the interception rate for the latter at an abysmal 29% amid Kyiv’s persistent shortage of Patriot interceptor missiles.

SBU Says Ukraine Struck Aircraft Plant in Crimea, Russian Port, Major Oil Refinery — Ukraine said it launched a sweeping overnight drone offensive targeting an aircraft plant in occupied Crimea, a strategic Black Sea port, and one of Russia’s largest oil refineries. The attacks coincided with strikes on Wildberries logistics hubs and drone alerts across several Russian regions.

Drapaty Orders Halt to Assault Regiment Recruitment — Ukrainska Pravda reported that assault regiments were instructed to suspend personnel replenishment from July 26, citing four sources familiar with the order.

Zelensky Reveals Ukraine and Russia’s Wartime Death Tolls — President Zelensky said around 50,000 Ukrainian service members have been killed and 400,000 wounded in the full-scale war. He estimated Russia’s total military casualties at 1.6 million, including approximately 700,000 killed.

Poland Officially Confirms Russian Kh-101 Missile Crashed on Its Territory — Poland’s deputy defense minister confirmed that the missile that entered Polish airspace was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile. Officials said about 20 Russian missiles had been heading toward Poland before being intercepted over Ukraine.

Why Putin’s Ratings Are Falling Despite Polling Manipulation — Fuel shortages, worsening economic sentiment, and Ukrainian strikes are making the war harder for ordinary Russians to ignore. As Putin offers no quick solution, even loyal citizens are beginning to withdraw their support.

Ukrainian Drones Send Crimea’s Tourism Industry Into Freefall — Ukraine’s summer drone campaign is taking a growing toll on occupied Crimea’s economy, with tourism collapsing, hotels sitting empty, and businesses struggling amid repeated strikes, power outages, and fuel shortages as visitors increasingly stay away.

In an Odesa Cafe — At the Cafe Central in Odesa, a young server asked me when I thought the war would end. I didn’t have any exclusive insight then, and I still don’t. But I do know what can be done to end it sooner rather than later.

Putin Ready to Sacrifice Crimea Chief Aksyonov as Crisis Deepens, Partisans Say — Ukrainian partisan movement Atesh claims the Kremlin has decided to remove Russian-installed Crimea chief Sergei Aksyonov after the September elections. Russian-appointed interior minister Alexei Dmitriev is reportedly a leading candidate to replace him.

Ukraine Downs Russian ZALA Recon Drone at Record Altitude of 21,000 Feet — Ukrainian forces have shot down a Russian ZALA Z-20 reconnaissance drone at an altitude of 21,000 feet, marking one of the highest successful drone interceptions of the war. The UAV, designed to operate beyond the reach of most counter-drone systems, was destroyed over southern Ukraine.

Ukraine Sends Firefighters to Help France Battle Wildfires — Ukraine has sent 70 firefighters and 15 specialized vehicles to France to help battle wildfires, with officials saying additional assistance, including aircraft, could be provided if needed.

French Delegation Visits Kyiv ReabiCentre Treating Ukrainians With Severe War Injuries — French officials reviewed a joint rehabilitation project at Kyiv’s National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopaedics. The ReabiCentre provides free, high-tech treatment and can assist more than 1,000 wounded service members annually.

Trump Still Not ‘Sure’ about Granting Patriot Production License to Ukraine — Trump said he has not decided whether Ukraine will be allowed to produce Patriot interceptor missiles, appearing to soften an earlier commitment made after meeting President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Zelensky Asks Trump to Get Musk’s OK for Starlink-Guided Strikes Inside Russia — Ukraine has asked President Donald Trump to persuade Elon Musk to allow Starlink to guide Ukrainian drone strikes inside Russia, according to The Atlantic. President Volodymyr Zelensky reportedly argued the move would help target Russian missile launchers as Kyiv faces dwindling supplies of Patriot interceptors.

Poland: Escalating Xenophobia Towards Ukrainians — Following an attack on a Ukrainian couple in Wrocław, commentators in Poland and Ukraine warn of rising anti-Ukrainian hostility. They urge political leaders to condemn hate, counter prejudice fueled by propaganda and political rhetoric, and call for stronger EU involvement to address growing xenophobia and protect affected communities.

Moscow Region Publishes Bomb Shelter Maps as Long-Range Strike Fears Grow — Authorities in Russia’s Moscow region have begun publishing official maps of bomb shelters, reversing a previous policy of withholding the information. The move comes after criticism over a lack of air raid alerts during recent Ukrainian drone attacks and amid warnings that Kyiv could soon field longer-range ballistic missiles.

‘Reckless’ Russia Condemned as Missile with ‘Significant’ Payload Crashes in Poland — A Russian cruise missile that crossed into Polish territory and crashed in a field contained a “significant” amount of explosives, prosecutors have said, while NATO condemned the incursion as “yet another reckless act by Russia.”
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, July 29, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on July 30, 2026

Ukraine’s Drone Campaign Hits Russia’s ‘Wartime Amazon’ in Volgograd and Tatarstan — Drone attacks reportedly hit Wildberries facilities in Volgograd and Tatarstan, extending Ukraine’s campaign against logistics hubs accused of supporting Russia’s military supply system.

From Radushne to Lublin: How Russia’s North Korean Missiles Expose the West’s Air Defense Gap — Russia’s apparent return to using North Korean ballistic missiles – alongside a missile breach of Polish airspace – shows that Ukraine’s air defense shortage is already a direct threat to Europe.

Witkoff, Kushner Expected in Kyiv for First Visit Around Independence Day — US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to make their first visit to Kyiv around Ukraine’s Independence Day celebrations.

Crimea Bridge Closed as Explosions Rock Occupied Peninsula — Russian occupation authorities temporarily shut the Kerch Bridge early Friday amid reports of explosions and drone activity across occupied Crimea, including Sevastopol.

Russian Boxers Cleared to Compete Under National Flag and Anthem — World Boxing has fully reinstated Russian athletes, permitting them to compete under the national flag and anthem after restrictions imposed following Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Russian Missile Destroys US-Owned Drone Factory in Kyiv — A Russian ballistic missile destroyed a Kyiv drone factory owned by Delaware-registered Terminal Autonomy, marking what appears to be the first time Moscow has targeted a US military-related company throughout the whole war. No casualties were reported in the strike.
